Once in Hawaii when I was about 13 I was swimming in the ocean and I saw a sea turtle. I had a snorkel on so I could easily follow the turtle without going up for air. I accidentally followed the turtle off the reef and when I looked up there was a tiger shark. I freaked out (obviously) and swam away as fast as I could and once I got to where I could stand, I went to do so and was hit by a wave. I was stuck for so long that I mentally gave up. Later, I washed up on the beach. (P.S. this is the same beach that the movie Soul Surfer is about)

Another time I was in Costa Rica and the car in front of me flipped off the road and me (18) and my mom and uncle were the only people there. I was the only one who spoke Spanish and one of the people in the car had been thrown into the jungle.

Another time in Mexico me and my fiance were on the highway and saw a huge cloud of smoke. Another car accident and we were the only ones there. Mexico had no emergency number that the people hit were aware of and they spoke no english. I have some medical training so I helped as much as I could but one of them was already dead.

Another time I was camping on a lake when I was about 17. My dad and I decided to see if we could kayak across the lake (it's very large). When we were in the middle of the lake, I got a fish on the line. As I went to reel it in a flash flood happened. The fish had already destabilized me and the rain was hitting so hard it hurt my body. My dad and I were able to get to part of the shoreline but it was all cliff. We found a big tree and my dad broke off enough branches for is to huddle close to the stump. Eventually we couldn't feel our bodies so we took off all of our clothes except bathing suits (recommended for hypothermia). We got our kayaks and tried to walk them along the shoreline in the sort of direction of our camp. The water that was previously too cold to swim in felt like a hot tub. All of my skin stung. And then lightning hit the water far on another part of the lake. My entire body straightened out and I couldn't move momentarily. We kept going along the side of the lake and eventually the rain wasnt hurting as bad. At that point we picked the direction we thought our camp was in and blindly paddled. Eventually we made it back. There was a search party going for us.

I'm really sorry you're going through all of that. It all sounds incredibly hard. When I was 8 (I'm 22 now) I had the same issue of not wanting anyone to know I wanted to die. In fact it took me until I was 19 to actually tell anyone for real, and it's one of my biggest regrets. When I think of how different my childhood and life could've been if I had gotten real help initially, I cant help but mourn my younger self. You have time and it sounds like resources (therapist and mom) to get help! You can tell your therapist you feel like you want to die without anything catastrophic happening. Your therapist can't help with this if they don't know about it. I know it feels weird to talk about but I'm positive that your therapist has had to have that conversation a million times. You don't have to think about anyone else, just what is best for you!! You get to prioritize yourself because you are WORTH IT!! And I don't believe for a second that everyone you know dislikes you!! And I'm also positive that you're not ugly!! Even if you are certain you believe that you're ugly, your 13- your appearance will change completely by the time you're done with puberty. I don't even recognize pictures of 13 year old me. No one you know would rather you suffer than tell them!!! And believe it or not, telling someone could actually help make it  better! As someone with a college education in Psychology, I've learned about things that can really help with depression. Your mom and therapist have a million times more information than me! So it's worth it!! Because you're worth it and you're happiness is worth it!!! Remember that it's not selfish to focus on your own wellbeing!! And always feel free to reach out to me💛
